item.title: NASA sent 12.5M tomato seeds to space in 1984; by 1990, 40,000 schools in 40 countries grew them
item.description: In 1984, NASA initiated the SEEDS project aimed at exploring how the space environment affects plant growth. Participants, comprising approximately 3.3 million students from diverse educational backgrounds worldwide, received kits that included seeds launched into space and Earth-based controls for comparison. Preliminary findings indicated a marginally enhanced germination rate for the seeds sent to space, though notable growth differences diminished during the plants' life cycles.

item.title: Retired UK rail engineer turns East Sussex garden into 50-foot railway with solar-powered trolley
item.description: Adrian Backshall transformed his East Sussex garden into a working railway, inspired by his railway engineering career. The garden features a unique 50-foot railway with a solar-powered system and authentic railway memorabilia. Initially a lockdown project, it has evolved to include a Victorian-style carriage for entertaining guests. Backshall's project reflects a blend of history and engineering, following his retirement from Network Rail.

item.title: 14 Kazakh military personnel killed during naval exercise; five officers detained
item.description: In a heartbreaking turn of events, 14 servicemen from Kazakhstan tragically perished during a naval exercise hindered by harsh weather conditions. In the aftermath, five defense officials were detained over alleged negligence regarding navigation protocols. Rescue teams bravely recovered three soldiers from the Caspian Sea. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has declared a national day of mourning to pay tribute to those who lost their lives.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Covid test company executive pleads guilty to billing insurers $500 M for services never provided
item.description: A Fast Lab executive pleaded guilty in a COVID-19 testing fraud case involving over $500 million in allegedly false claims. Prosecutors said the company used customers’ insurance information to bill government-backed healthcare programmes for COVID-19 testing services that were never provided. Seyhun admitted helping submit fraudulent claims and agreed to forfeit $4.31 million.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California crews uncover possible 45-million-year-old ‘thunder beast’ fossils in Oceanside
item.description: Fossilised bones from a large hoofed mammal were uncovered during an excavation project in Oceanside, California. Paleontologists are studying the remains, which may belong to a thunder beast or a swamp rhino. The discovery took place approximately 12 feet below the surface in the Santiago Formation's sedimentary rock. Researchers are working to determine the exact identity of the fossils found during construction.

item.title: Recall alert: 43,674 light-up children’s toys sold for $1 from 2016 to 2026 are being recalled due to ingestion and chemical burn risk
item.description: Attention parents: approximately 43,674 light-up children's toys have been recalled due to dangerous battery compartments that children can easily access. This recall affects light-up glasses, crown headbands, sparkle headbands, and light-up ties sold from September 2016 to May 2026. Please ensure your children stop using these items and contact ABC Trading to obtain a refund. Dispose of these toys following local hazardous waste protocols.

item.title: Georgia landowner's $23 million tax claim over 103 acres cut to $480,000 by court
item.description: A Georgia landowner claimed a $23 million charitable tax deduction after donating a 103-acre conservation easement, arguing the property could have been used as an aggregate quarry. The US Tax Court rejected the proposed quarry use, valuing the easement at $480,000. The 11th Circuit upheld the valuation and a 40% gross valuation misstatement penalty.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Belgian quarry uses solar panels and sheep in a project to produce clean power
item.description: A quarry in Florennes, Wallonia, is implementing an agrivoltaic project that integrates solar panels with sheep farming. This project installs 3,240 photovoltaic panels over 3.3 hectares, allowing sheep to graze underneath. It will generate 2.33 GWh of electricity annually, with some used by the quarry and surplus supplied to the public grid. The initiative aims to reduce the quarry's carbon footprint and support local agriculture.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ukraine strikes Russian oil refinery, train in overnight drone attacks; 2 killed
item.description: Russian governor Yuri Slyusar said around 50 drones were destroyed over the region and the strike forced the refinery to temporarily suspend operations. He said there were no reports of casualties there. In Ulyanovsk, eight people were injured after another drone attack damaged industrial and civilian infrastructure, Governor Alexei Russkikh said. The region is home to a major electronics plant.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Colorado researchers grow world’s priciest spice on solar panels, doubling yield and earning $60,000
item.description: A study by Colorado State University reveals that saffron flourishes under semi-shaded solar panels, yielding better results than those without shade. By integrating rooftop farming with renewable energy, urban food production can tackle space constraints. Projections suggest considerable net revenue from saffron and electricity production in five years, although challenges related to installation and upkeep remain for successful implementation.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Oregon buys 92-foot Abiqua Falls after fears it could be sold to a private owner
item.description: Oregon has approved a $2 million purchase of Abiqua Falls, a famous 92-foot waterfall that was put up for sale by its private owner in February. The deal includes 160 acres of land and will bring the waterfall under state ownership, while officials work on plans for management, maintenance and public access.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 51,000 reclining chair batteries recalled after reports of fires
item.description: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission has recalled approximately 51,000 lithium-ion battery packs from Blue Cactus Company. These battery packs, sold on Amazon, pose risks of overheating and potentially catching fire. Consumers who purchased the recalled packs should immediately stop using them and contact the company for replacements. Proper disposal methods are required due to the fire hazard associated with these batteries.
